result:
I now have the full picture end to end. Here's how it works.

## Write side: keeping the index in step

Editing an issue title goes through the `updateIssueAction` server action (`src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`), which checks `issue:update` permission and then calls `updateIssue()` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`. That function re-fetches the current row, asserts org scope and that the issue isn't archived, persists the change via `issueRepo.updateIssue(input)`, and — critically — calls `emit("issue.updated", { orgId, issueId, projectId, changedFields, ... })` from `src/lib/event-bus.ts` (issue-service.ts:99).

The event bus (`emit` in `event-bus.ts`) is an in-process typed pub/sub: it looks up every subscriber registered for `"issue.updated"` and runs them via `Promise.allSettled`, so one failing handler can't break another or fail the write itself. Subscribers are attached once at process start by `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts` (invoked from `src/instrumentation.ts`), which calls `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts` among others.

`registerSearchListeners()` subscribes a handler to `"issue.updated"` that does **not** trust the event payload's title — it re-reads the issue by ID (`issueRepo.findIssueById(payload.orgId, payload.issueId)`) and, if found, calls `indexIssue(orgId, issue)`. This "re-read rather than trust the payload" pattern means a partially-applied write is never indexed as if it succeeded. `indexIssue` builds the searchable text as `[issue.title, issue.description ?? ""].join("\n")` and calls `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument(orgId, "issue", issue.id, content, issue.projectId)` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`.

`upsertSearchDocument` writes into the denormalised `search_index` table (defined in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`), keyed by `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)` rather than by row id — it looks for an existing row with that triple and either updates its `content`/`projectId`/`indexedAt` or inserts a new row. That row is what's stored: `id`, `orgId`, `projectId`, `subjectKind` (`"issue" | "comment" | "project"`), `subjectId`, the concatenated `content` string, and `indexedAt`. There's no separate title/body field — the title is just line 1 of `content`, which is how `search()` later derives a title for display (`row.content.split("\n")[0]`).

So the full write-time chain is: `updateIssueAction` → `updateIssue` (issue-service.ts) → `emit("issue.updated")` (event-bus.ts) → the `"issue.updated"` listener in `registerSearchListeners()` (search-service.ts) → `issueRepo.findIssueById` (re-read) → `indexIssue` → `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument` (search-repository.ts). This is fully synchronous/awaited within `emit`, so by the time `updateIssueAction` returns, the index row is already updated — there's no async queue or delay, which is why a colleague searching "moments later" already sees it. (Separately, `search-reindex-job.ts`'s `runSearchReindexJob` exists to rebuild an org's whole index from scratch after bulk imports or drift, walking projects/issues/comments and calling the same `indexIssue`/`indexComment`/`indexProject` functions, but that's not on the normal edit path.)

## Read side: what a query goes through

The command palette (`SearchDialog` in `src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx`) debounces keystrokes, parses the raw string with `parseSearchQuery` (`query-syntax.ts`) — which only interprets `kind:`/`project:` prefixes when the client already believes `advanced_search` is on — and calls the `onSearch` prop, wired to `searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts`.

`searchAction` runs through `withAction`, which resolves the actor and validates input against `searchQuerySchema` (`src/schemas/search.ts`). It then does its own `can(actor, "org:read", ...)` check and re-derives the `advanced_search` flag via `isEnabled` (`src/lib/feature-flags.ts`) using `buildFlagContext`, narrowing `kinds` to `["issue"]` if the org's plan/role doesn't have the flag — degrading gracefully rather than erroring — before calling `search(actor, input)` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

`search()` in `search-service.ts` performs, in order:
1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` (`src/lib/tenant.ts`) — throws `TenantScopeError` if the actor's org doesn't match the query's org.
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))` (`src/lib/permissions.ts`) — throws `PermissionDeniedError` if the actor lacks read access.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) — a per-org token bucket (120 capacity, 60/min refill at baseline, scaled by plan). **This is the circumstance under which a perfectly valid-looking query is refused**: if the bucket is empty, `verdict.allowed` is `false` and `search()` throws `Error("Search rate limit reached; try again after ${verdict.resetAt}")` — nothing wrong with the query itself, the org has just searched too often too fast.
4. It re-checks `advanced_search` server-side (via `isEnabled` again, independently of the client/action check) and, if the query text contains a `:` while the flag is off, throws `"Field-scoped search is not included in this plan"` — a second refusal path, this time about query *syntax* rather than *rate*, guarding against a client that lies about having advanced search enabled.
5. Only after all four gates pass does it call `searchRepo.searchDocuments(input)`.

`searchDocuments` in `search-repository.ts` builds a Drizzle query filtered by `orgPredicate(searchIndex.orgId, input.orgId)` (tenant isolation — this is the filter the module comment calls "what actually matters here"), a `like(searchIndex.content, '%q%')` substring match (deliberately simple, not a real full-text engine), optional `subjectKind`/`projectId` filters, then paginates with keyset pagination (`_paging.ts` helpers) ordered by `indexedAt`/`id` descending. Back in `search-service.ts`, each returned row is mapped into a `SearchHit` — title from `content.split("\n")[0]`, a `snippetAround()` excerpt centered on the match, and an `href` from `hrefFor(subjectKind, subjectId)` — and returned as a paged result to the dialog for rendering.
